story: I Was a Warehouse Wage Slave: Inside the online-shopping shipping machine
text: >I would be curious about the energy needs per unit, though. An 180 lb person speed walking at 5 mph burns 650 Calories/hr. That's 80¢/shift in electricity. But that's not the big savings. Humans need lights and air-conditioning – robots don't. [VIDEO]
Sounds like Amazon is telegraphing its intentions for increasing automation in warehouses, a la Zappos. [VIDEO]

Self-driving cars + robot arm + bufferbox = extremely cheap, fully automated delivery service. Add a robotic distribution center [VIDEO] and you have an automated Amazon competitor. If, on top of that, Google turns your Google account into a bank account, you'll be able to buy literally with one click. Google's dominance in mobile with Android will ensure that everyone has a Google bank account through which you can make most of your purchases. If you're a manufacturer, Google will take care of all your advertising for free, just so long as you give them a tiny cut of each sale. Google will be a trillion dollars company.

story: Google Is Building A Same-Day Amazon Prime Competitor, “Google Shopping Express”
text: KIVA Systems' robots ( [LINK] ) revolutionized warehouse automation. Zappos was using KIVA when Amazon acquired Zappos, and then Amazon acquired KIVA for $775 million. See "Autonomous Robots Invade Retail Warehouses" ( [LINK] ) KIVA @ Zappos: [VIDEO] I doubt Amazon is going to permit a contract between KIVA and Google so it will be interesting to see Google's innovations in this space.
